key_insight: ST2M guides crystal generation with crystallographic symmetry, improving the yield of structures that are simultaneously stable, unique, and novel.
engineering_relevance: Generating candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints could accelerate materials screening and reduce wasted downstream calculations.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Condition discrete–continuous diffusion on Wyckoff patterns and apply degree-of-freedom masks.
Use a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 96.37% structural validity, a 23.86% stable–unique–novel yield for known patterns (68.15% relative improvement over the best baseline), and 21 previously unreported stable structures identified by first-principles calculations among selected candidates.
watch_item: First-principles validation covered selected low-predicted-energy candidates; the abstract does not quantify performance on unknown Wyckoff patterns.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
